blocks.prompt: 18. If \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}\) and \(\frac{1}{c}\) are in A.P., show that the common difference is \(\frac{a - c}{2ac}\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof. In an A.P. the common difference \(d\) is the gap between neighbours.
We must write \(d\) using \(a\) and \(c\) only (no \(b\)).
Plan: write \(d\) in two ways and add them, so that \(\frac{1}{b}\) cancels.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}, \frac{1}{c}\) are in A.P.
To prove: \(d = \frac{a - c}{2ac}\).
Method: \(d = \frac{1}{b} - \frac{1}{a}\) and \(d = \frac{1}{c} - \frac{1}{b}\).

Write the common difference twice
\[d = \dfrac{1}{b} - \dfrac{1}{a} \quad (1)\]
\[d = \dfrac{1}{c} - \dfrac{1}{b} \quad (2)\]
Why: Second minus first, and third minus second, are both equal to \(d\).

Add (1) and (2)
\[2d = \dfrac{1}{c} - \dfrac{1}{a}\]
Why: \(+\frac{1}{b}\) and \(-\frac{1}{b}\) cancel; this removes \(b\).

Simplify
\[2d = \dfrac{a - c}{ac}\]
\[d = \dfrac{a - c}{2ac}\]
Why: Common denominator \(ac\): \(\frac{a}{ac} - \frac{c}{ac}\); then divide by 2.

Check with numbers
\(a = 1,\ c = 3\) (so \(b = \frac{3}{2}\) from Question 17):
\[d = \dfrac{2}{3} - 1 = -\dfrac{1}{3}\]
\[\dfrac{a - c}{2ac} = \dfrac{1 - 3}{6} = -\dfrac{1}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both ways give the same \(d\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: the common difference is \(\frac{a - c}{2ac}\).
